p0.original: 关键问题：谁最容易受到应激的影响
p0.en: Key issue: Who is most vulnerable to stress

p2.original: 人格特征影响个体对应激情境的反应，从而影响其暴露于潜在的应激源时感到的痛苦程度。
p2.en: Personal characteristics affect the individual's response to passion and thus the degree of suffering that he or she feels when exposed to potential stressors.

p3.original: 有些人在经历了“9·11”事件或失去所爱之人这类创伤性事件后能够重振旗鼓，而有些人会被一些微不足道的日常小麻烦压垮，这是为什么呢？我们感受到的压力不仅受应激情境的性质和强度的影响，还受我们如何诠释应激源的影响。在这一学习阶段中，我们将重点关注影响应激反应的人格特征。这一学习阶段的核心概念概括了将要学习的内容：
p3.en: What is the reason why some people who have experienced the events of 11 September or have lost their loved ones to traumatic events can be revived and some people will be crushed by a few small daily problems? The pressures we feel are influenced not only by the nature and intensity of the response to the passions, but also by how we interpret the sources of the response. During this learning phase, we will focus on personality characteristics that influence stress. The core concept of this learning phase outlines what will be learned:

p4.original: 人格特征影响个体对应激情境的反应，从而影响其暴露于潜在的应激源时感到的痛苦程度。
p4.en: Personal characteristics affect the individual's response to passion and thus the degree of suffering that he or she feels when exposed to potential stressors.

p5.original: 在深入探讨相关研究之前，我们想介绍一个关于应激与疾病关系的模型，它将是本章随后内容的指导。
p5.en: Before further exploring the relevant studies, we would like to present a model of the relationship between stress and disease, which will guide the subsequent contents of this chapter.

p6.original: 图14-9展示了这个模型的可视化图像，表明应激源如何导致了应激，而应激又如何导致身心疾病。在进一步阅读本书之前，请认真查看这幅图。看看你能否弄清楚每一组因素是如何在应激与疾病的关系中发挥作用的，并根据图中的提示加深理解。
p6.en: Figure 14-9 shows visual images of the model, showing how stress causes stress and how stress causes physical and mental illness. Before further reading this book, please look carefully at this map. See if you can figure out how each set of factors works in the relationship between stress and disease, and understand it better in the light of the hints in the figure.

p7.original: 注意这个模型中有两次实施干预的机会：一次位于应激源与应激之间，另一次位于应激与疾病之间。换句话说，一组因素可以防止应激源使我们感受到应激，另一组因素可以防止应激引发身心疾病。我们称前者——可以干预应激源和应激之间关系的因素——为缓解因素（moderator），因为我们感知到的应激水平受它们的调节或控制。这类因素大多数是认知评估概念中的变量。换句话说，我们对应激源的判断和解释受这些缓解因素的影响。在此先举一个例子，探讨这一系列可能的干预措施。
p7.en: Attention is drawn to two opportunities for intervention in this model: one between stress and stress, and the other between stress and disease. In other words, a set of factors can prevent stress from being felt, while a set of factors can prevent stress from causing physical and mental illness. We call the former — factors that can interfere with the relationship between stress and stress — a mitigating factor, because our perceived levels of stress are regulated or controlled by them. Most of these factors are variables in the concept of cognitive assessment. In other words, our judgement and interpretation of the sources of stress are influenced by these mitigating factors. To give an example, this set of possible interventions is explored.

p8.original: 图14-9 个体因素如何影响应激反应
p8.en: Figure 14-9: How individual factors influence stress

p9.original: 想象一下这样的场景：德米提雅（Demetria）和克里（Cory）刚结完婚，正在规划着未来的生活。他们希望尽快买房子，拥有属于自己的家。然而，他们最近开始为一些问题而争吵，因为他们对目标的展望截然不同。德米提雅乐观地认为，他们能够在一年内支付房子的首付款，并相信只要他们认真理财，一定能达成目标。克里就没那么乐观了，在他看来，似乎每当自己接近目标时，就总会有一些事情阻碍他，他相信这次也会发生相同的事情。对他来说，“靴子总会掉下来”，他担心如果他们对一年内买到房子抱太大的期望，就难免会失望。
p9.en: Imagine the fact that Demetria and Cory are just getting married and planning for the future. They want to buy a house as soon as possible and have a home of their own. However, they have recently begun to argue over a number of issues, as their vision of the Goals is very different. Demetria was optimistic that they would be able to pay down payment for the house within one year and was confident that they would achieve the goal if they managed their finances carefully. Kerry was not so optimistic, and it seemed to him that whenever he approached the target, there was always something that stood in his way, and he believed that the same thing would happen. For him, “tits will always fall”, and he fears that if they expect too much to buy a house in a year, they will inevitably be disappointed.

p10.original: 你是否在这个例子中看到了你自己或者你认识的某个人的影子？如果人们长期用某种方式来感知和处理事件，具有跨情境一致性，并且与其他人的方式相似，我们便称之为人格特质。我们来探讨一下人格特质对应激源与应激之间关系的影响。
p10.en: Did you see yourself in this example or someone you knew? We call it a character if people have a long history of understanding and dealing with events in a way that is consistent across circumstances and similar to others. Let's look at the impact of the relationship between personality and stress.

p12.original: 14.5 将A型人格和敌意与心脏病相联系。
p12.en: 14.5 Link A personality and hostility to heart disease.

p13.original: 14.6 比较内控者和外控者的健康相关结果。
p13.en: 14.6 Compare health-related outcomes of both internal and external controls.

p14.original: 14.7 评估坚韧性、乐观主义和韧性对应激的积极影响。
p14.en: 14.7 Assess the positive impact of resilience, optimism and resilience.

p17.original: 将A型人格和敌意与心脏病相联系。
p17.en: Linking A personality and hostility to heart disease.

p18.original: 当心脏病专家梅尔·弗里德曼和雷·罗森曼（Meyer Friedman & Ray Rosenman，1974）找人来修理候诊室中的家具时，对方注意到了医生们不曾注意到的东西：大多数椅子的前部边缘的磨损程度异常严重。当医生们意识到这一点时，他们想知道病人的心脏问题是否与他们应对应激的特定方式有关，就像他们总是坐在座位的边缘一样。由此医生们开启了一系列的研究来检验他们的假设，对病人的访谈揭示了一个令人惊讶的共同行为模式。多项研究结果反复表明，病人面对应激的反应是不耐烦、具有竞争性、攻击性和敌意。许多病人也承认他们是出了名的工作狂。最终，弗里德曼和罗森曼发现，上述态度和行为的结合不仅与心脏病相关，而且能够准确预测心脏病。他们称这种模式为A型人格模式，而拥有B型人格模式的人的生活方式很放松。A型人格者罹患心脏病的风险是B型人格者的两倍（Matthews，1982）。
p18.en: When the cardiologists Mel Friedman and Ray Rosenman, 1974 found someone to repair the furniture in the waiting room, they noticed something that the doctors had not noticed: the front edges of most chairs had been worn to a very severe degree. When doctors are aware of this, they wonder whether the heart problems of patients are related to the particular way they respond to stress, as they always sit on the edge of a seat. As a result, doctors began a series of studies to test their assumptions, and interviews with patients revealed an amazing common pattern of behaviour. Multiple studies have repeatedly shown that patients are impatient, competitive, aggressive and hostile in the face of stress. Many patients also admit that they are well known workaholics. Ultimately, Friedman and Rosenman found that the combination of these attitudes and behaviour was not only related to heart disease, but also capable of accurately predicting heart disease. They refer to this model as the A personality model, while those who have the B personality model have a relaxed way of life. Type A persons are twice as at risk of heart disease as Type B persons (Matthews, 1982).

p19.original: 从最开始确定A型人格（Type A）以来，进一步的研究表明，正是A型人格中普遍存在的愤怒和敌意增加了个体患心脏病的风险。而时间紧迫感、完美主义和竞争意识本身都不是风险因素。充满敌意的人更缺乏信任、易怒，更具有敌对性。或许你注意到了敌意与认知评估的联系，确实，怀有敌意的人比一般人更有可能感知到威胁。这种思维方式使得他们难以维持人际关系，这反过来又减少了他们可获得的社会支持。敌意还与吸烟、饮酒和暴饮暴食等各种危害健康的行为有关联。这些行为本身就增加了个体罹患心脏病的风险（Taylor，2008）。
p19.en: Since the initial determination of Type A personality (Type A), further studies have shown that it is the anger and hostility prevalent in Type A personality that increases the risk of individual heart disease. The sense of time urgency, perfectionism and the sense of competition are not risk factors in themselves. Those who are hostile are more lacking in trust, anger and hostility. Perhaps you have noticed the link between hostility and cognitive assessment, and it is true that people who are hostile are more likely than the general population to feel the threat. This way of thinking makes it difficult for them to maintain relationships, which in turn reduces the social support available to them. Animosity is also associated with various health-related behaviours such as smoking, drinking and drinking. These acts in themselves increase the risk of heart disease among individuals (Taylor, 2008).

p21.original: 从生理学角度看，敌意强的人在面对潜在的应激源时唤醒更快，而且表现出更高的唤醒水平，并且一旦应激源过去，他们的唤醒水平恢复正常水平所需要的时间更长（Fredrickson et al.，2000；Guyll & Contrada，1998）。敌意还与较高水平的细胞因子有关，这可以延长应激反应（Niaura et al.，2002）。然而，研究人员还不能确定，这些生物学上的差异是天生的，还是部分由童年环境造成的，比如在充满冲突且接纳和支持程度较低的家庭中长大的男孩更容易产生敌意（Matthews et al.，1996）。目前的研究普遍认为，先天和后天因素都在敌意及心脏病的形成中发挥一定的作用。显然，敌意会通过多种途径导致个体患心脏病。
p21.en: From a physiological point of view, hostile people wake up faster and display higher levels of awakening in the face of potential stressors and, once the stressors pass, take longer to restore their levels of awakening (Fredrickson et al., 2000); Guyll & Contractor, 1998. The hostility is also associated with higher levels of cytological factors, which can prolong stress (Niaura et al., 2002). However, researchers are not yet certain whether these biological differences are born or partly caused by childhood environments, such as boys growing up in conflict-ridden families with low levels of acceptance and support (Matthews et al., 1996). Current research generally suggests that both congenital and acquired factors play a role in the formation of hostility and heart disease. It is clear that hostility can cause individual heart disease in many ways.

p22.original: 需要明确的是，虽然很多人时常会感到愤怒，但正常的愤怒与敌意人格之间有重要的区别。当面对消极的情境时，我们都会感到愤怒，这样的愤怒是健康的，甚至具有适应性：它暗示我们出问题了，并为我们提供能量以采取措施改变情境。正常的愤怒与敌意人格的愤怒形成了鲜明的对比，后者是一种长期的敌意行为模式，在很多情况下会频繁发作。另一个区分因素是唤醒的程度：当一辆缓慢行驶的车辆挡住了你的路，你感到愤怒是合理的，但暴怒就是不理性的表现，并且很危险，尤其当这成为你生活中的一个常见模式时。
p22.en: It needs to be made clear that, while many are often angry, there is an important difference between normal anger and hostile personality. When faced with a negative situation, we all feel anger, which is healthy and even adaptive: it implies that we are in trouble and provides us with the energy to take measures to change the situation. Normal anger contrasts sharply with animosity, which is a long-term pattern of hostile behaviour, which in many cases occurs frequently. The other distinguishing factor is the level of awakening: when a slow-moving vehicle blocks your way, you are right to be angry, but anger is irrational and dangerous, especially when it becomes a common pattern in your life.

p23.original: 不仅心血管疾病，其他疾病也与A型人格有关联，如过敏、伤风、头痛、胃病和单核细胞增多症（Suls & Marco，1990；Suls & Sanders，1988）。同样，A型人格的完美主义倾向与焦虑障碍（试图达成不可能完成的目标）和抑郁症（未能达成目标）有关（Joiner & Schmidt，1995）。
p23.en: Not only cardiovascular diseases, but other diseases are also associated with type A personality, such as allergies, flu, headaches, stomach disease and mononucleocytes (Suls & Marco, 1990); Suls & Sanders, 1988. Similarly, the idealistic tendency of the A personality is linked to anxiety disorder (in an attempt to achieve an impossible goal) and depression (in a failure to achieve the goal) (Joiner & Schmidt, 1995).

p24.original: 理解敌意和心脏病以及其他A型人格行为与相关健康风险之间的关系，有助于开发出更有效的疾病预防措施。规律的有氧运动、放松训练，甚至是一项旨在帮助怀有敌意的人放慢说话的速度和学会小声说话的项目，都能有效地降低他们罹患心脏病的风险（Taylor，2008）。然而，全面的应激管理训练能够带来极大的好处。研究表明，接受了应激管理训练的心脏病患者，在经历发作并幸存下来后，在接下来的3年里心脏病再次发作的比率是未接受应激管理训练的对照组的一半（Friedman & Ulmer，1984）。研究人员总结道：“在预防心脏病复发上，任何药物、饮食或运动计划，甚至连心脏搭桥手术的效果都无法与学会管理应激相媲美。”因此，即使在生命早期出现了A型人格行为并持续到成年期，仍然可以通过精心设计的干预措施有效地帮助A型人格者改变他们的生活方式。A型人格和B型人格个体的关键特征比较见表14-1。
p24.en: Understanding the relationship between hostile and heart disease and other type A personality behaviour and related health risks helps to develop more effective disease prevention. Regular aerobics, relaxed training, and even a project designed to help hostile people slow down their speech and learn to whisper, can effectively reduce their risk of heart disease (Taylor, 2008). However, comprehensive stress management training can bring great benefits. Studies show that heart disease patients who have been trained in stress management, after having experienced and survived an outbreak, the rate of re-incident in the next three years is half that of the control group that did not receive stress management training (Friedman & Ulmer, 1984). The researchers concluded: “No drug, diet or sports programme, even a heart bridging operation, can be compared with the learning to manage stress when it comes to preventing the recurrence of heart attacks. Thus, even if type A personality behaviour occurs early in life and continues into adulthood, it can be effective in helping people of type A personality to change their way of life through carefully designed interventions. A comparison of the key characteristics of the individuals with the A personality and the B personality is shown in Table 14-1.

p29.original: 比较内控者和外控者的健康相关结果。
p29.en: Compare health-related outcomes of both internal and external controls.

p30.original: 你有多大信心能让生活变成你想要的样子？在前面的例子中，新婚夫妇克里和德米提雅出现的分歧体现了他们在心理控制源（locus of control）上的差异，心理控制源是人格的一个维度，这是一种相对稳定的预期模式，对影响自己生活中事件结果的能力的期望。
p30.en: How much confidence do you have in making life what you want? In the preceding example, the differences between newlyweds Kerry and Demetria reflect their differences in the sources of psychological control (local of control), which is a dimension of personality, a relatively stable pattern of expectations and expectations of the ability to influence the outcome of events in their lives.

p31.original: 内控者（internals）通常认为如果他们采取某种行动，就很可能获得他们期待的结果。例如，勤奋学习便会取得好成绩。
p31.en: Internal controlrs (internals) usually believe that if they do something, they are likely to get the results they expect. For example, hard-working learning can achieve good results.

p32.original: 外控者（externals）则与之相反，认为自己的努力与结果之间的关系是不可预测的。他们更有可能相信自己无法控制的因素，比如他们的成绩更多取决于考试的公正性或者老师是否喜欢他们，而不是学习的刻苦程度。
p32.en: In contrast, external control (externals) perceives the relationship between their efforts and results as unpredictable. They are more likely to believe in factors beyond their control, such as their performance, which depends more on the fairness of the examination or whether the teacher likes them than on the degree of hard work of learning.

p33.original: 面对应激事件时，与外控者相比，内控者更可能认为应激源是可控的，这会减轻应激，并最终带来各种健康的结果。至少在某种程度上，对控制力的感知是可以习得的：“9·11”事件期间，接受了此类灾难培训的消防员和其他工作人员患创伤后应激障碍的概率较低（Perrin et al.，2007）。
p33.en: In the face of stress events, internal regulators are more likely than outsiders to consider stress sources as manageable, which reduces stress and ultimately leads to various health outcomes. At least to some extent, perceptions of control can be learned that firefighters and other staff trained in such disasters were less likely to suffer from post-traumatic stress disorder during the events of 11 September (Perrin et al., 2007).

p34.original: 14.6.1 心理控制源、健康与长寿
p34.en: 14.6.1 Sources of psychological control, health and longevity

p35.original: 三十多年前，研究人员在美国康涅狄格州（Connecticut）的一家疗养院进行了一项经典研究，阐明了个体感知到的控制力对健康的重要性。疗养院某一层的老年人对自己的日常生活拥有多种选择权。例如，他们可以选择是否及何时观看电影，房间里的家具和个人物品如何摆放，是否要在房间里摆放植物等，不过他们需要自己给植物浇水。在与住在这层楼的老年人的沟通中，养老院的工作人员强调了老年人年要对自己的生活满意度负责，工作人员很乐意根据他们的需求提供帮助（如挪动家具）。而住在另一层的老年人作为对照组，他们在健康和年龄等重要特征上与上一组匹配。对于对照组的老年人，他们的生活起居全部由工作人员负责，如给植物浇水、安排电影放映时间和根据管理人员的决定摆放家具。
p35.en: More than 30 years ago, researchers carried out a classic study at a nursing home in Connecticut, United States, which illustrated the importance of individual perceptions of control to health. Older persons at one level of the sanatorium have multiple options for their daily lives. For example, they can choose whether and when to watch the film, how to place the furniture and personal effects in the room, whether to plant in the room, etc., but they need to water the plant themselves. In communication with older persons living on this floor, the staff of the nursing home emphasized that the elderly were responsible for their own satisfaction with their lives and were willing to provide assistance (such as moving furniture) in accordance with their needs. Older persons living in another layer are considered as control groups, matching the previous group with important features such as health and age. For the older persons in the control group, their living is the sole responsibility of the staff, such as watering plants, scheduling film shows and putting furniture on the basis of the decision of the manager.

p36.original: 结果会怎样？18个月过后，与对照组的老年人相比，承担更多个人责任的老年人更主动、更敏锐、更幸福。令人意想不到的是，心理控制源还影响了老年人的寿命。在研究结束时，对照组的死亡率比承担更多个人责任组的死亡率高67%（Rodin，1986）。
p36.en: What happens? After 18 months, older persons with more personal responsibilities are more proactive, sensitive and happy than those in the control group. Surprisingly, psychological control also affects the longevity of older persons. At the end of the study, the mortality rate in the control group was 67 per cent higher than that in the more individually responsible group (Rodin, 1986).

p37.original: 各种与健康相关的结果都受心理控制源的影响。除了更有可能系安全带、有规律的运动、注意饮食等对健康有明显好处的行为之外，内控者的免疫系统比外控者的更好（Chen et al.，2003）。他们很少生病，从疾病和手术中康复得更快（Skinner，1996）。更重要的是，强烈的内控感实际上消解了社会阶层和健康之间的关系：具有内控倾向的低收入个体和高收入个体一样健康（Lachman & Weaver，1998）。
p37.en: Health-related outcomes are influenced by sources of psychological control. In addition to the more likely combination of seat belts, regular sports, dietary care, and other behaviours that have a clear health benefit, the immune system of the internal control is better than that of the external control (Chen et al., 2003). They rarely get sick and recover faster from illness and surgery (Skinner, 1996). More importantly, the strong sense of internal control has in fact eliminated the relationship between social class and health: low-income individuals with a controlled tendency are as healthy as high-income individuals (Lachman & Weaver, 1998).

p38.original: 14.6.2 文化对心理控制源的影响
p38.en: 14.6.2 Impact of culture on psychological control sources

p39.original: 对文化的研究表明，东西方文化在心理控制源感知上存在一个有趣的区别。
p39.en: Studies on culture show that East-West culture has an interesting difference in the perception of the source of psychological control.

p40.original: 初级控制（primary control）在西方文化中比较普遍，我们在前文中也探讨过：这是一种采取行动以控制外部事件的方式。
p40.en: Primary control is more common in Western cultures, and we have also explored earlier: it is a way to take action to control external events.

p41.original: 东方文化更倾向于次级控制（secondary control），这是一种强调控制个人对事件的反应的方式（Rothbaum et al.，1982）。
p41.en: Eastern culture prefers secondary control, which is a way of emphasizing control of individual reactions to events (Rothbaum et al., 1982).

p42.original: 一种文化的普遍价值体系影响了该文化中最受珍视和推崇的控制类型。例如，在日本传统的集体主义文化中，次级控制的发展源于养育子女的方式。孩子们被教导要根据情境调整自己的反应，以维持社会和谐。这与个人主义文化中养育子女的方式形成鲜明的对比，个人主义文化鼓励人们控制情境本身。研究表明，这两种策略在各自的文化背景下都很有效（Weisz et al.，1984）。此外，当初级控制失败或个人无法采取初级控制时，进行次级控制可改善健康。
p42.en: The universal value system of a culture affects the most valued and favoured types of control in that culture. For example, in Japan's traditional collectiveist culture, the development of secondary control stems from the way in which children are raised. The children are taught to adapt their responses to the situation in order to maintain social harmony. This is in stark contrast to the way children are raised in an individualistic culture that encourages people to control the situation itself. Research has shown that both strategies are effective in their respective cultural contexts (Weisz et al., 1984). In addition, secondary control improves health when primary control fails or when individuals are unable to take primary control.

p43.original: 14.6.3 心理控制源是先天的还是习得的
p43.en: 14.6.3 Sources of psychological control are natural or acquired

p44.original: 虽然心理控制源的确在早期就会出现，且具有遗传的特点，但我们的期望也会受经历的影响。如果个体试图逃离具有威胁的情境却反复经历失败，那么最后他们便不再尝试，这一概念被称为习得性无助（learned helplessness）。马丁·塞利格曼（Martin Seligman）和他的同事们进行的动物研究是习得性无助的最初证据。当狗在无处可逃的情况下遭受电击后，它们很快就放弃了逃避电击的尝试，被动地听从命运的安排（Seligman，1975，1991；Seligman & Maier，1967）。即使后来有机会逃避电击，通常这些狗什么也不做，只是忍受电击带来的痛苦。与之相比，之前没有受过惩罚的对照组的狗很快就逃跑了。塞利格曼得出结论，实验组的动物已经知道，它们所做的一切都无关紧要，也无法逃避电击，所以它们被动地接受了自己的命运（Seligman & Maier，1967）。
p44.en: While it is true that the sources of psychological control will emerge early in life and have genetic characteristics, our expectations will also be influenced by experience. If individuals try to escape a threatening situation and experience repeated failures, then they end up not trying, a concept known as leened helplessness. The animal research carried out by Martin Seligman and his colleagues was the first evidence of lack of assistance in learning. When dogs were subjected to electric shocks in circumstances where there was no escape, they quickly abandoned their attempts to escape electric shocks and passively listened to fate arrangements (Seligman, 1975, 1991); Seligman & Maier, 1967. Even if there was a subsequent opportunity to escape the shock, the dogs usually did nothing but endure the pain caused by the shock. In contrast, dogs who had not previously been punished had quickly escaped. Seligman concluded that the animals of the team had learned that everything they did was irrelevant and could not escape electric shocks, and that they had accepted their fate passively (Seligman & Maier, 1967).

p45.original: 唐纳德·西罗多（Donald Hiroto，1974）在人类被试身上也进行了习得性无助实验，该实验是塞利格曼所做的实验的变体。学生们被安排在一个噪声非常大的房间里，有些学生找到了关闭噪声来源的方法，但对其他学生来说，噪声开关坏了。后来学生们被安排进另一个房间里，房间里充满另一种烦人的噪声。那些先前找到关闭噪声来源方法的学生很快就在第二个房间里找到了解决办法。相比之下，先前没能找到关闭噪声来源方法的学生只是坐在第二个房间里，并没有尝试去阻止新应激源。他们已经习得了无助感。塞利格曼和其他学者在不同的人群中都发现了习得性无助症状，包括因受虐待而沮丧的儿童、遭受家庭暴力的女性、受折磨的战俘（Overmier，2002；Yee et al.，2003）。相反，无论何种职业、技能水平高低，如果允许人们对他们所处的环境和工作条件进行一定程度的控制，他们的幸福感都会更高（Faulkner，2001；Zarit & Pearlin，2003）。
p45.en: Donald Hiroto, 1974, also carried out an incipient helplessness experiment on the human body, a variant of an experiment made by Séligman. The students were placed in a very loud room, and some found ways to shut down the source of the noise, but for others the noise switch was broken. The students were later placed in another room, filled with another annoying noise. Those who had previously found ways to shut down the noise sources quickly found a solution in the second room. In contrast, students who had not previously been able to find ways to shut down the sources of noise sat in a second room and did not try to stop the new sources of stress. They've learned to feel helpless. Séligman and other scholars have found symptoms of acquired sexual helplessness among different groups of people, including children frustrated by abuse, women victims of domestic violence and prisoners of war who have been tortured (Overmier, 2002); Yes et al., 2003). On the contrary, regardless of occupation, skill level, they are more happy if they are allowed to exercise some degree of control over their environment and working conditions (Faulkner, 2001); Zarit & Pearlin, 2003.

p46.original: 因此，尽管我们可能生来就容易受到内部或外部控制倾向的影响，但我们的经历也起到了一定的作用。对“9·11”事件救援人员的研究和习得性无助的研究只是证明这一重要事实的两个领域。
p46.en: Thus, while we may have been born vulnerable to internal or external control tendencies, our experience has also played a role. The study of relief workers from the events of 11 September and the study of unhelpful learning are just two areas that bear witness to this important fact.

p47.original: 14.7 坚韧性、乐观主义和韧性

p49.original: 评估坚韧性、乐观主义和韧性对应激的积极影响。
p49.en: Assess the positive impact of resilience, optimism and resilience.

p50.original: 缓解应激最有效的因素是坚韧性（hardiness），其基础是个体对应激的态度以及如何管理应激。与A型人格行为相比，坚韧性是一种能够促进健康应对的人格特征。“坚韧性”一词最早出现于20世纪70年代和80年代的一项大规模研究中，该研究对美国伊利诺伊州贝尔电话公司（Illinois Bell Telephone，IBT）的管理者进行了调查。萨尔瓦多·麦迪（Salvatore Maddi）和来自芝加哥大学的研究团队在几年的时间里，从该公司管理者那里收集了大量的数据。当时美国联邦政府对公共事业的放松管制措施导致IBT大规模裁员，工作条件、职位和预期经常发生变化，工作环境充满了应激。三分之二的管理者经历了消极的健康后果，包括心脏病、中风、抑郁和焦虑障碍。另外三分之一的管理者也处于相同的工作环境下，他们不但没有生病，反而看起来精神抖擞（Kobasa et al.，1979；Maddi & Kobasa，1984）。事实证明，导致这一差异的因素被称为“坚韧性”，这个概念包含三个特征（见图14-10），现在被称为“坚韧性态度”或“3Cs”（Maddi，2002）。
p50.en: The most effective mitigating factor for stress is resilience (hardness), based on individual attitudes to stress and how to manage stress. In comparison with type A personality behaviour, tenacity is a personality characteristic that promotes a healthy response. The term “resilience” was first introduced in a large study in the 1970s and 1980s that investigated the managers of the Illinois Bell Telephone, IBT, in Illinois, United States. Salvatore Maddi and the research team from the University of Chicago collected a large amount of data from the company's managers over the course of several years. At that time, the United States federal government's deregulation of public utilities had led to massive lay-offs of IBT, frequent changes in working conditions, positions and expectations, and a stressful working environment. Two thirds of managers experienced negative health consequences, including heart disease, stroke, depression and anxiety disorders. Another third of managers are in the same working environment, and instead of being ill, they appear to be in a trance (Kobasa et al., 1979); Maddi & Kobasa, 1984. The factor that led to this difference has proved to be known as “resistence”, a concept that encompasses three features (see figures 14-10) and is now referred to as “resistence” or “3Cs” (Maddi, 2002).

p51.original: 图14-10 坚韧性的三个特征（3Cs）

p52.original: 总之，这些坚韧性态度提供了勇气和动力，将工作中的应激转化为优势。我们可以把这些坚韧性因素应用到大学生的生活中。假设有一天你必须为一个重要的考试做准备，而此时一个朋友向你倾诉他遭遇了一个巨大的麻烦并请求你的帮助。这两个应激源——重要的考试和急需帮助的朋友，可能会让你不知所措，尤其当你的资源已经快耗尽时。但是一个具有坚韧性的人会运用“3Cs”来减轻应激：承诺（我要帮助我的朋友，也要准备考试，两者都不能放弃）；挑战（现在有两件重要的事需要我做，我有哪些选择可以同时满足这两种需求）；控制（我用一个下午的时间学习，晚餐时和朋友聊天。毕竟我需要吃饭来保持大脑的正常运转，然后在睡觉前再多复习一点内容）。
p52.en: In short, these tenacity provides courage and motivation to transform stress in the work into advantage. We can apply these resilience factors to the lives of college students. Suppose one day you have to prepare for an important examination, and a friend told you that he was in a great trouble and asked for your help. These two sources of stress — important examinations and friends in need of help — may confuse you, especially when your resources are running out. But a resilient person uses the 3Cs to reduce stress: promise (I want to help my friends and prepare my exams, neither can be abandoned); Challenges (two important things now need to be done, and what options do I have to meet both needs simultaneously); Control (I spend one afternoon studying, talking to friends at dinner. After all, I need to eat to keep my brain working and study a little bit more before I go to bed.

p53.original: 坚韧性已经被证明可以减少应激情境对人们的影响，比如商人、孩子、夫妻、大学生、奥运会运动员、军人和执法人员（Maddi，2002）。尽管坚韧性人格通常在生命早期就显现了出来，但就像控制源一样，坚韧性也可以通过后天习得。研究人员已经成功地开发了训练坚韧性的项目，通过解决问题（而不是逃避）、充满社会支持（而不是冲突）的互动以及有益的（而不是过度的）利己，帮助人们学习以更具适应性的方式来应对生活中的应激源。这一过程有助于加强他们的坚韧性态度，改善他们的表现、行为、动机和健康状况（Beasley et al.，2003；Maddi，1987，2002；Maddi et al.，1998；Maddi et al.，2009）。
p53.en: Retardability has proven to reduce the impact of passion on people, such as businessmen, children, couples, university students, Olympic athletes, military and law enforcement personnel (Maddi, 2002). Although a tenacity personality is usually visible at the early stages of life, it can be acquired through natural means, as is the control source. Researchers have successfully developed resilient training projects that help people learn to cope with the stressors of life in a more adaptive way by solving problems (rather than avoiding them), social support (rather than conflict) interaction and beneficial (rather than excessive) self-interest. This process contributes to strengthening their resilience and improving their performance, behaviour, motivation and health (Beasley et al., 2003); Maddi, 1987, 2002; Maddi et al., 1998; Maddi et al., 2009).

p55.original: 当考虑未来的时候，你通常会期待好事发生，还是担心事情可能出错？乐观主义者认为未来是光明的，在他们看来，“玻璃杯里还有半杯水”。而悲观主义者则没有那么积极，在他们看来，“玻璃杯只有半半水”。悲观主义不仅仅是习得性无助。心理学家马丁·塞利格曼（Seligman，1991）说，生活给予乐观主义者和悲观主义者同样的挫折和不幸，但乐观主义者更有能力承受它们。总而言之，乐观的人比悲观的人更少生病，患病后能更快地恢复，并且更健康、更长寿（Bennett & Elliott，2002；Taylor et al.，2000a）。是什么导致了这种差异？乐观主义（optimism）能直接影响健康，因为乐观主义者的情绪更积极，这能增强他们的免疫系统（Cohen et al.，2003）。此外，乐观的人会使用更积极的策略来应对应激，在本章的末尾我们将会讨论这一点。
p55.en: When you think about the future, do you usually expect good things to happen, or do you worry that things might go wrong? Optimists think that the future is bright and that, in their view, “there is still half a glass of water in the glass”. The pessimists are less active, and in their view, “the glass is half water”. Pessimism is more than mere inroads. Psychologist Seligman (1991) said that life gave optimists the same frustration and misfortune as pessimists, but optimists were better equipped to bear them. Overall, optimistic people are less ill than pessimists, recover faster after illness and live healthier and longer (Bennett & Elliott, 2002); Taylor et al., 2000a. What led to this difference? Optimism can have a direct impact on health, as optimists are more active, which enhances their immune system (Cohen et al., 2003). Moreover, optimistic people will use a more proactive strategy to respond to stress, which we will discuss at the end of this chapter.

p56.original: 塞利格曼和他的同事们（Seligman et al.，2002）进行的一项长期研究表明，乐观主义者会对消极事件做出三种特定的假设或归因（见表14-2）。
p56.en: A long-term study conducted by Seligman et al. 2002 and his colleagues showed that optimists make three specific assumptions or attributions to negative events (see table 14-2).

p57.original: 表14-2 乐观主义者对消极事件做出的特定归因
p57.en: Table 14-2 Specific attribution of negative events by optimists

p58.original: 塞利格曼是国际积极心理学协会（International Positive Psychology Association）的创始人之一，他相信人们可以习得乐观的思维方式。他建议，其中一种方法是在感到沮丧或无助时，用一种特定的方式与自我对话。塞利格曼说，积极的自我对话应该关注个人遭受挫折的意义和原因。例如，如果一个正在减肥的人吃了一块蛋糕，她不应该想“反正我已经毁了我的减肥计划，干脆吃掉整个蛋糕吧”，而应该这样想“我很喜欢吃蛋糕，但我知道在大多数时间里我都能坚持减肥计划”。塞利格曼认为，从本质上讲，通过采取建设性的思维方式、自我评估和行为规划，人们可以习得乐观的态度。
p58.en: Séligmann, one of the founders of the International Active Psychologic Association, believes that people can learn optimistic ways of thinking. He suggested that one approach would be to engage in a specific dialogue with oneself when frustrated or helpless. Séligman said that active self-dialogue should focus on the meaning and causes of individual setbacks. For example, if a man who is in the process of losing weight ate a piece of cake, she should not think, “I've ruined my diet, just eat the whole cake”, but think, “I love eating cake, but I know I can do it for most of the time”. Seligman believes that, in essence, optimism can be learned through constructive thinking, self-assessment and behavioural planning.

p59.original: 考虑到这一点，你可能会想起认知评估在应对应激中的重要性以及本章中关于应激反应存在个体差异的内容。以更积极的方式思考问题或更坚强的方式应对困难，可以改变我们对潜在应激源的理解，从而降低我们感知到的应激。
p59.en: With this in mind, you may recall the importance of cognitive assessment in coping with stress and the individual differences in stress in this chapter. Addressing difficulties in a more active way or in a stronger way can change our understanding of the potential sources of stress, thereby reducing the stress that we feel.

p61.original: 女演员克里斯蒂娜·艾伯盖特（Christina Applegate）所选的职业似乎让她的生活充满了魔力。1971年她出生于美国加利福尼亚好莱坞，母亲是一位演员兼歌手，父亲是唱片制作人。这位年轻美丽、才华横溢的女子在数十部电影、电视节目和百老汇舞台剧中担任女主角或女配角。她凭借精湛的演技赢得了无数奖项，拥有众多粉丝。她还主持过美国综艺节目《周六夜现场》（Saturday Night Live），并在2009年《人物》（People Magazine）评选的“最美丽的人”中名列榜首。
p61.en: The profession chosen by actress Christina Applegate seems to have given her a magical life. She was born in 1971 in Hollywood, California, United States of America, with her mother as an actor and singer and her father as a record producer. The young, beautiful and talented woman was the leading woman or a woman in dozens of films, television programmes and Broadway theatres. She has won countless awards and many fans with her fine acting skills. She also hosted the American fusion show Saturday Night Live, and was ranked first among the “Most Beautiful People” in the 2009 People Magazine contest.

p62.original: 然而在聚光灯之外，克里斯蒂娜的生活充满了各种巨大的压力。她的父母在她出生后不久就离婚了，她和第一任丈夫结婚几年后也离婚了，她的挚友兼前男友死于药物过量。一个月后，克里斯蒂娜被诊断患有乳腺癌，并接受了双侧乳房切除手术。因为发现得早，她的癌症痊愈了。媒体采访她时，问她当得知自己像母亲一样也患上乳腺癌时，她是如何应对困难的。她说，在得知初步诊断结果后，“我浑身发抖，然后，我很快就进入了‘顾全大局模式’”。在2010年接受《美国周刊》（US Magzine）网站采访时，克里斯蒂娜还表示，为了应对这种威胁生命的疾病，她的生活开始发生转变。“你马上就会变得有点疯狂，不让任何应激影响你的生活，不吃任何垃圾食品，生活发生了180度的大转变。你对生活的看法也发生了一些变化。”目前，她致力于通过自己的慈善基金会“女性采取正确的行动”（Right Action for Women），为癌症研究和治疗筹集资金。
p62.en: However, outside the spotlight, Christina's life was under enormous stress. Her parents divorced shortly after her birth, as well as a few years after her marriage to her first husband, and her close friend and ex-boyfriend died of overdose. A month later, Christina was diagnosed with breast cancer and was subjected to a double-sided breast mutilation. Because she found out early, her cancer was cured. When she was interviewed by the media, she asked how she had managed to cope when she learned that she had breast cancer, like her mother. She said that, after learning of the preliminary diagnosis, “I shivered, and then I quickly entered the `over-the-board model'”. In an interview with the American Weekly (US Magzine) website in 2010, Christina also stated that her life had begun to change in response to this life-threatening disease. "You're going to get a little crazy, not to let any stress affect your life, not to eat any junk food, and life is going to change a lot 180 degrees. There have been some changes in your perception of life. At present, she is working to raise funds for cancer research and treatment through her own charitable foundation, Right Action for Women.

p63.original: 克里斯蒂娜·艾伯盖特的生活充满了成功和挫折。这是运气使然吗？心理学家认为，在克里斯蒂娜的决定、态度和行为中，相比天赋或基因，有一种东西对于幸福感而言更宝贵：韧性（resilience）。
p63.en: The life of Christina Aborgheit is full of successes and setbacks. Is this luck? Psychologists believe that there is something more valuable in Christina's decisions, attitudes and behaviour than a gift or gene for happiness: resilience.

p64.original: 韧性是指一种不管个体在成长过程中面临何种严重的威胁，都能适应、应对应激和获得幸福的能力（Masten，2001）。事实上，“韧性”这个词来自拉丁语词根“buoyant”，字面意思是“在波浪中跳跃”。近二十多年，大多数有关韧性的研究都集中在儿童和青少年群体。他们要应对生活中各种充满应激的情境，可能包括父母的忽视或虐待、父母的精神障碍、丧亲之痛以及其他严重的风险因素。面对相同的情境，为什么有些孩子患病或遭遇失败，而有些孩子不仅存活下来，甚至获得了成长与成功？
p64.en: Resilientness is the ability to adapt, respond to stress and achieve happiness, regardless of the serious threat to individual growth (Masten, 2001). In fact, the word “resistence” comes from the Latin root word “buyant”, which literally means “jumping in waves”. For almost two decades, most of the studies on resilience have focused on children and youth groups. They address the full range of stressful situations in life, which may include parental neglect or abuse, parental mental disorders, loss of family and other serious risk factors. In the same situation, why are some children ill or failed while others not only survive, but even grow and succeed?

p66.original: 即使在很小的时候，有韧性的孩子也会表现出突出的特质。他们往往拥有更高的认知能力、更强的责任心、更好的社交技能、更强的竞争力并能获得更好的养育资源（Masten，2001；Riolli，2002）。生命早期出现的韧性特质支持了一种推断：韧性是一种天生的特性。然而最近，研究人员开始转而关注成年人的韧性及韧性是否可以被习得。
p66.en: Even at a very young age, resilient children display outstanding qualities. They tend to have greater cognitive capacity, greater responsibility, better social skills, greater competitiveness and access to better parenting resources (Masten, 2001); Riolli, 2002. The early emergence of resilience characteristics supports the inference that resilience is a natural characteristic. Recently, however, researchers have begun to turn to the question of whether adults ' resilience and resilience can be learned.

p67.original: 一项关于成年人韧性的研究对1999年前南斯拉夫科索沃冲突中的幸存者进行了调查。结果发现，韧性与一些人格特质的组合有关，包括外倾性、尽责性和乐观主义（Riolli，2002）。其中，乐观主义对人们变得更有韧性和减少脆弱性特别有帮助。此外，你可能已经注意到，韧性似乎与坚韧性有些重叠。这两个概念的确存在关联。坚韧性集中在三个特征上，但韧性包含了更广泛的特质。而且，由于坚韧性可以在特定训练项目的帮助下得到发展，也许未来我们对韧性可能也会有类似的发现。
p67.en: A study on adult resilience investigated survivors of the 1999 conflict in Kosovo, the former Yugoslavia. As a result, resilience was found to be associated with a combination of personality characteristics, including external leaning, due diligence and optimism (Riolli, 2002). Optimism, among other things, has been particularly helpful in making people more resilient and reducing vulnerability. In addition, you may have noticed that resilience seems to overlap with resilience. The two concepts are indeed linked. Resilientness is concentrated on three characteristics, but resilience encompasses a wider range of features. Moreover, since resilience can be developed with the help of specific training projects, perhaps in the future we may have similar findings.

p68.original: 哥伦比亚大学的心理学家乔治·博南诺（George Bonanno）是研究丧亲和创伤领域的先驱人物。他对在个人丧失和重大灾难中遭遇了极端应激的幸存者（从儿童到成年人）进行广泛的纵向研究和访谈研究，由此得出的结论是，在成年之后的不同时期，韧性始终保持在一般水平（Bonanno，2009）。在这些研究的基础上，博南诺发现，在面对巨大的应激时，与长期功能障碍或延迟创伤相比，韧性和坚韧性更常见。我们可以合理地推断，无法很好地应对新的应激源的人或者已经处于高度应激状态的人，假若遭遇了另一个应激源，那么他们将处于一般适应性综合征的第二阶段。
p68.en: George Bonanno, a psychologist at Columbia University, was a pioneer in the field of mourning and trauma. He has conducted extensive longitudinal and interview studies of survivors (from children to adults) who have experienced extreme stress during individual loss and major disasters, which have led to the conclusion that resilience remains at the general level at different stages of adulthood (Bonanno, 2009). On the basis of these studies, Bonano found that resilience is more common in the face of enormous stress than long-term functional impairments or delayed trauma. It is reasonable to assume that people who are unable to cope well with new sources of stress, or who are already in a state of high stress, would be in the second stage of a general adaptive syndrome if they were to experience another source of stress.

p69.original: 从表14-3里，你可以发现博南诺的研究中更多的细节。
p69.en: From Table 14-3, you can find more details in Bonano's study.

p71.original: 博南诺还创造了“丑恶应对”（coping ugly）这一术语，用来指各种在充满应激的情境中很有用，但在正常情境下可能不合适的应对策略。丑恶应对包括自我提升偏差、自我吹捧、大笑和微笑、思维抑制及持有无论如何都能生存下来的信念等。他的主要观点是，大多数人几乎都能很好地应对任何事情，我们通过自己开发的一系列应对策略来做到这一点。这也解释了为什么人类几乎可以应对所有的挑战（Bonanno & Mancini，2008）。
p71.en: Bonano also created the term “coping ugly” to refer to various coping strategies that are useful in stressful situations, but may not be appropriate in normal situations. Ugly responses include self-promoting biases, self-proclaiming, laughs and smiles, inhibitions of thinking, and the belief that it can survive in any case. His main point is that most people are almost able to respond well to anything, and we do so through a series of coping strategies that we have developed. This explains why humanity can meet almost all of the challenges (Bonanno & Mancini, 2008).

p72.original: 因此，韧性并不罕见。事实上，许多英雄和“无名英雄”在我们不知情的情况下克服了重重困难。他们应对痛苦和挑战的能力实际上不是超凡力量的结果，而是源于平凡的魔力。这是韧性研究人员安·马斯顿（Masten，2001）在描述正常的适应过程时所使用的术语，她认为，正是韧性使人们能够取得比预期更好的结果。因为期待更好的结果，或许我们在生活中会变得更乐观，也变得更有韧性。
p72.en: So resilience is not rare. Indeed, many heroes and “unknown heroes” have overcome difficulties without our knowledge. Their ability to cope with pain and challenges is not in fact the result of extraordinary power, but rather of the magic of ordinaryity. This is the term used by the resilient researcher Masten 2001 in describing the normal adaptation process, and she believes that it is resilience that enables people to achieve better results than expected. Because we look forward to better results, perhaps we will become more optimistic and resilient in life.

p73.original: 心理学很有用 运用心理学来学习心理学
p73.en: Psychology is useful. Use psychology to learn psychology.

p74.original: 想象一下，你刚刚遭遇了一种丧失：一个朋友挑起争端，并且侮辱了你，辜负了你对他的信任；你爱的人没有回应你的情感；你的宠物死了，尽管朋友们劝你应该“熬过去”，你依旧感到十分悲痛。无论经历了什么样的应激，你都不知道该和谁聊一聊——但你还是强烈地感到有必要把自己内心的想法和感受表达出来。你能够做什么呢？你可以先把它们写下来。在此过程中，你会对自己的心理状态有更多的了解。
p74.en: Imagine that you have just suffered a loss: a friend who has provoked a dispute and has insulted you and failed you in your trust in him; The person you love doesn't respond to your emotions; Your pet is dead, and you're still very sad, despite the advice of your friends that you should get through it. Whatever stress you have experienced, you have no idea who to talk to — but you still feel strongly about the need to express your thoughts and feelings inside. What can you do? You can write them down first. In the process, you'll know more about your mental state.

p75.original: 为什么要写出来？为什么不大吼大叫，把痛苦从身体里发泄出来呢？其中一个原因是，当带着攻击性发泄情绪时，对于缓解应激的作用不大，也于健康无益。相反，它可能会使痛苦加剧，或者带来有害的影响（Gross & Psaki，2004；Smythe，1998）。而写下你的担忧和丧失对你的情绪有治疗性的效果（Pennebaker，1990，1997；Zimmerman，2002）。研究还发现，促进免疫功能紊乱患者写下其担忧和感受对康复有促进作用（Pennebaker，1997）。当你写下自己的想法和感受时，你只是在和自己交流，也是为自己发声。你无须在听众面前表演，也无须取悦听众，你可以敞开心扉，把一切都说出来，放心吧，你不需要解释任何事情。你所需要的只是一个场地、一段时间、一些材料以及下决心保持这个习惯。以下几种方法可以使这件事更容易、更有效。
p75.en: Why would you write it? Why don't you yell and let the pain out of your body? One reason for this is that when offensive emotions are carried out, they are not very effective in mitigating stress and do not contribute to health. Instead, it may increase suffering or have harmful effects (Gross & Psaki, 2004); Smythe, 1998. And write about your fears and loss of therapeutic effects on your emotions (Pennebaker, 1990-1997); Zimmerman, 2002. The study also found that promoting the writing of fears and feelings by patients with immunological disorders has contributed to rehabilitation (Pennebaker, 1997). When you write your thoughts and feelings, you just communicate with yourself and speak for yourself. You do not have to perform in front of the audience, nor to please the audience, and you can open your heart and say everything. Don't worry, you don't have to explain anything. All you need is a place, a period of time, some material and a determination to keep this habit. The following approaches could make the matter easier and more effective.

p76.original: 你可以在任何媒介上写作，只要对你来说是舒适的、便利的。你可以在键盘上打字，但你不一定总有计算机在手。手写更能表达个人情感，而且你不需要写得十分工整——因为只有你能看到它。通过使用纸笔，你不仅可以书写，还可以画画或涂鸦，以非文字的方式表达自己。而且小小的笔记本不贵，也便于随身携带。
p76.en: You can write on any medium, as long as it's comfortable and convenient for you. You can type on the keyboard, but you don't always have a computer. Handwritten is more personal, and you don't have to write very well -- because you're the only one who can see it. By using paper and pens, you can write, draw or graffiti, and express yourself in non-textual terms. And the little notebooks are not expensive, and they are easy to carry with them.

p77.original: 开始写之前选择一个主题。如果是丧失或担忧促使你进行写作练习，那就从这些主题开始。如果没有，那么选择一个可以激发你对生活中重要挑战的情感和想法的“任务”。一位教授要求学习了丧失的心理学学生写一篇有关丧失的日记，包括个人的丧失或令人难忘的事件，如恐怖袭击或名人的死亡，以及这对写作者意味着什么（Harvey & Hofmann，2001）。
p77.en: Select a theme before you start writing. If loss or concern prompts you to practice writing, then start with these themes. If not, choose a “mission” that inspires your feelings and thoughts about the important challenges of life. A professor asked the lost psychologist to write a journal about loss, including personal loss or memorable events, such as terrorist attacks or the death of a celebrity, and what that meant for the author (Harvy & Hofmann, 2001).

p78.original: 把你的想法和感受都写下来，并专注于寻找困难经历中的意义。你也许不知道问题的答案（为什么我们的关系没能维持下去），但你可以推理和想象（也许现在正是我独处的好时机）。治疗性写作或谈话的一个重要目的是获得洞察力、实现成长和改变。把记忆像讲故事一样写下来也会有所帮助：故事要有开头、中间和结尾，对人物和事件进行描述，以及你对“故事的真谛”的总结和学到的教训（Harvey et al.，1990；Murray，2002）。
p78.en: Write down your thoughts and feelings and focus on finding meaning in difficult experiences. You may not know the answer to the question (why our relationship has not been sustained), but you can reason and imagine (perhaps now is my good time alone). An important purpose of therapeutic writing or conversation is to gain insight, achieve growth and change. Writing memories like stories can also help: stories have their beginnings, middles and endings, descriptions of people and events, and your summary of the “truth of the story” and lessons learned (Harvey et al., 1990); Murray, 2002.

p79.original: 利用空闲的时间写作，设定目标，比如每周写几页。把自己当作记者，记录任何看起来重要的细节（DeSalvo，2000）。尝试各种形式的写作，比如写情书或分手信。勇于发现糟糕的事情的另一面，或者将你正在做的各种事情进行分类，如为别人所做的事情和为自己所做的事情（Zimmerman，2002）。
p79.en: Use free time to write, set targets, such as a few pages per week. I'm a journalist and I'm a journalist and I'm a journalist and I'm a journalist and a journalist. Attempting to write in various forms, such as love letters or break-up letters. Be brave to discover the other side of a bad thing, or to classify what you are doing, for what others do and for what they do (Zimmerman, 2002).

p80.original: 坚持下去。让写作成为一种习惯，而不仅仅是困难时期的一种释放。研究人员发现，如果只写创伤经历会加深痛苦，让人更难以敞开心扉或渡过难关。所以，即使有时候你感觉很好、不需要书写的时候，也要写几行，因为这些文字会让你记得自己曾经感受到愉悦，并提醒自己是如何做到的。
p80.en: Hold on. Let writing become a habit, not just a release from difficult times. Researchers have found it more difficult to open up or to get through a traumatic experience alone. So, even when you feel good and don't need to write, write a few lines, because these words remind you of the pleasure you've felt and remind you how you did it.

p81.original: 你写作的目标并不是为了成为伟大的作家（虽然也有可能），而是克服压力，了解你的反应和应对模式，并帮助你康复。通过设定目标和制定规则，你可以思考如何运用你在这一学习阶段所学的关于感知和坚韧性的知识。通过写作，我们可以学会以一种更具适应性的方式感知应激源。此外，还记得我们在本章的第一个核心概念中探讨过叙述的重要性吗？不过别让写作练习给你带来太大的压力！这些写作任务由你自己决定，这样你就可以放心，它既没有截止日期的压力，也不用担心成绩好坏。
p81.en: Your writing is not intended to be a great writer, although it is possible, but rather to overcome the pressures, to understand your response and response patterns and to help you recover. By setting goals and setting rules, you can think about how to apply the knowledge you have learned about perception and resilience at this learning stage. By writing, we can learn to feel the sources of stress in a more adaptive way. In addition, remember the importance of narratives that we have explored in the first core concept of this chapter? But don't let writing practice put too much pressure on you! These writing tasks are up to you, so you can rest assured that it has no deadline pressure and does not have to worry about good or bad grades.
